title: ARCH↔DEVOPS-001: OTA/Orchestration Strategy + Pipeline & Artifact-Signing Feasibility
description: The Embedded Systems Architect provides the OTA (Over-the-Air) strategy (A/B partitions, signing, rollback), the gateway-orchestration approach (K3s/balena), build/toolchain constraints, and the deployment topology; the DevOps/Platform Engineer provides pipeline and fleet-management feasibility, the OTA implementation, the artifact-signing mechanism, and observability hooks. Grounded in EMBEDDED_SYSTEMS_ARCHITECT_SKILL §6.7 and DEVOPS_PLATFORM_ENGINEER_SKILL §6.5. The artifact-signing mechanism and any anti-rollback change are security-baseline-relevant (ESC-SEC; binding decisions under DEVOPS↔SEC-001 / FW↔SEC-001); OTA dispatch governance stays in the MLOPS↔DEVOPS-001 chain.

ota_orchestration_strategy.description: ARCH→DEVOPS: OTA strategy, gateway orchestration, build/toolchain constraints, deployment topology.

devops_feasibility.description: DEVOPS→ARCH: pipeline/fleet feasibility, OTA implementation, artifact-signing mechanism, observability hooks.

signing_baseline_change.description: True when the signing/anti-rollback baseline would change — fires ESC-SEC.

security_review_ref.description: Required when signing_baseline_change = true (Security Engineer review).

x-macp.tier_rationale: OTA/orchestration strategy and build/toolchain constraints are architecture decisions ratified by humans. The artifact-signing mechanism and anti-rollback posture touch the security baseline — a change there fires ESC-SEC and is bound under DEVOPS↔SEC-001 / FW↔SEC-001; OTA dispatch governance stays in the MLOPS↔DEVOPS-001 chain.
x-macp.cadence: TRIGGER (OTA and fleet-strategy alignment at planning; CI/CD integration during development; ADR consultation on any reliability/automation/security gap; production-scaling review)
confirm_conditions: the OTA strategy (A/B, signing, rollback) and orchestration approach are specified
pipeline/fleet feasibility verdict is stated with the OTA implementation reference
a signing/anti-rollback baseline change carries a Security Engineer review reference (ESC-SEC)
observability hooks are enumerated for fleet management
reject_conditions: an artifact-signing or anti-rollback baseline change accepted without a Security Engineer review reference (security baseline — ESC-SEC)
an OTA strategy change decided in this contract without an ADR (OTA governance is ADR-gated)
a pipeline presented as FEASIBLE while the signing mechanism weakens the security baseline (Honesty Over Polish §10.3)
counter_conditions: ALWAYS escalate ESC-SEC when the coordination changes the signing/anti-rollback baseline — propose, do not auto-confirm; the Security Engineer owns the binding decision
an orchestration/toolchain change implies a deployment-topology change — request an ADR before freezing the strategy
